cohort: 10,314 women with singleton gestations who had a routine second-trimester ultrasound at 17-23 weeks gestational age from 2010 to 2013
finding: Women with uterine fibroids may be at higher risk for a short cervix and several adverse obstetric and neonatal outcomes, including preterm delivery, primary cesarean, breech presentation, lower birth weight infants, and lower Apgar scores.
mod_finding: This study found that the presence of uterine fibroids was associated with an increased risk of preterm delivery, primary cesarean section, and breech presentation.
